about: Maps changed paths to the checks that should run. Read by select-checks.mjs. Rules are tried in order and the first match wins, so more specific rules come first. A path no rule matches is NOT ignored: a source file triggers the conservative set in `unknown`. Update this file in the same change that adds a new area to the repo.

unknown.why: No rule covers this path, so the selector cannot say what it affects. It asks for everything CI would run, rather than for nothing.

limitations: This plan is a recommendation computed from file paths. It cannot see runtime data (the engine reads artifacts/**/*.json and the player pool when it runs), so engine-adjacent changes carry explicit rules.
Direct-test selection finds tests that import a changed file. A change can break a test that only reaches it through other modules; the `related` checks cover that, at a higher cost.

Local PGlite is a single PostgreSQL session (version 18; CI runs 16). It cannot show locks, deadlocks or true concurrency, and parallel database runs fail for unrelated reasons. Only GitHub CI is authoritative for those.
Local results are not CI results. A plan is only complete when GitHub's required `test` job has passed on the pull request and `deploy` was skipped.

scope.label: Confirm the scope of the change
scope.note: Right branch and worktree (never switch a shared checkout), and the diff is exactly the intended files. No scratch file is staged or committed.

tc-ui.label: UI typecheck (tsc -b)
tc-ui.note: Never use `tsc -p .` in ui-source: it does not follow project references and passes vacuously.

engine-realism.label: Engine realism guard (league rates against the NFL)

stat-guard.label: Passing, rushing, scoring and sack statistics across 6 leagues
stat-guard.note: Compares with a baseline measured on seeds 101-124; if a deliberate change moves the averages, re-measure the baseline in the same commit.

circuits.label: Whole-season walkthroughs through the stage wiring
commands: npx vitest run --root online test/full-circuit.test.ts test/annual-circuit.test.ts test/humans-only-circuit.test.ts

visibility.label: Unrevealed results are never sent to a GM who has not watched them
visibility.prerequisite: A PostgreSQL on :5433 (`npm run online:db`, leave it running).
visibility.note: Run one file at a time on PGlite. Without a database this suite skips, and a skip is not a pass.

db-suites.label: Database-backed suites
commands: npx vitest run --root online --no-file-parallelism test/concurrency.test.ts test/commissioner-away.test.ts test/commissioner-transfer.test.ts test/hot-seat.test.ts test/inbox-facts.test.ts test/lobby.test.ts test/password-reset.test.ts test/poll-unchanged.test.ts test/vacate-advances.test.ts test/vacate-seat.test.ts test/result-visibility.test.ts
db-suites.prerequisite: A PostgreSQL on :5433 (`npm run online:db`, leave it running).
db-suites.note: Run one file at a time on PGlite. A pass here says nothing about locks, deadlocks or concurrency; CI's PostgreSQL does.

launcher-tests.label: Local league server launcher: database choice, scrubbed environment, loopback binding, readiness and cleanup
commands: npx vitest run --root online test/local-launcher.test.ts test/harness-redirects.test.ts
launcher-tests.note: Starts its own in-memory PGlite and a real league server on free loopback ports, and runs the HTTP harness against servers that redirect; needs no database from you.

infra-checks.label: Database test helpers, global setup and the no-DDL-in-suites guard
commands: npx vitest run --root online test/require-database.test.ts test/schema-setup.test.ts test/no-schema-in-suites.test.ts

how-it-works-test.label: How It Works text matches the mechanics it states

how-it-works-review.label: If a mechanic changed, ui-source/src/state/howItWorks.ts changes in the same commit
how-it-works-review.note: CLAUDE.md: the player-facing explanation of every system must stay true.

selector-tests.label: Verification tooling's own tests (selector, verdict, runner, safety, replay)
commands: npx vitest run test/verify-selector.test.ts test/verify-verdict.test.ts test/verify-safety.test.ts test/verify-replay.test.ts test/verify-output-signals.test.ts
selector-tests.note: Includes tests that run vitest and a repository clone of the git commands; the longest is the one proving an exported production DATABASE_URL never reaches a run.

related-engine.label: Every engine test that reaches the changed files (transitive)

related-ui.label: Every UI test that reaches the changed files (transitive)
related-ui.note: Runs inside ui-source so it uses the UI project's own vitest and config.

related-online.label: Every online test that reaches the changed files (transitive; with a database, one file at a time)
related-online.prerequisite: A PostgreSQL on :5433 (`npm run online:db`, leave it running).
related-online.note: The import graph decides which online tests run, and it can reach any of the database suites through db.ts, the league modules or the UI rules the server shares. Those suites return early without a database and a runner counts that as a pass (199 passed, 1 skipped, no database touched), so every transitive online run is a database check: it counts only if a database was used, and is not run without an explicit test database. Serial, because a local PGlite is one session.

full-online.label: Full online suite (with a database, one file at a time)
full-online.prerequisite: A PostgreSQL on :5433 (`npm run online:db`, leave it running).
full-online.note: About a dozen of these suites return early without a database and a runner counts that as a pass, so this run only counts as the full online suite when a database was really used. Run it with a test database; without one it is not run and the plan stays incomplete. Serial, because a local PGlite is one session.

league-metrics.label: Full league calibration against 2018-2025 NFL aggregates
league-metrics.note: Long. Run for any change to how units affect a play.

stress-smoke.label: Franchise stress test, smoke mode (three seasons plus a replay)
stress-smoke.note: Uses the mock backend, not the real engine. Not a Vitest run: it prints its own summary and sets its exit code. It writes its files to a scratch directory outside the repository, chosen by the runner.

preview-ui.label: Look at the change in a browser
preview-ui.note: Presentation changes are not covered by tests.

arcade-verify.label: Run standalone arcade verification explicitly (attestation)
arcade-verify.note: Run npm --prefix arcade run verify for arcade typecheck, unit tests, build and browser tests. Confirm only after observing every check succeed. This is a manual attestation, not independently observed runner evidence. The command allowlist is unchanged; standard CI and the franchise browser job do not run arcade tests. Linux arcade browser execution remains unverified until separately approved CI wiring exists.

static-review.label: Read the whole diff of the CI/deploy file
static-review.note: There is no YAML or Actions linter on this machine, so syntax and deploy conditions are only proven by GitHub running the workflow.

ci-pr.label: GitHub CI on the pull request
ci-pr.note: Open a PR into master. The required `test` job must pass and `deploy` must be skipped. This, not any local run, is the authoritative result.

ci-repeat-db.label: Re-run the pull request's CI at least three times
ci-repeat-db.note: Lock, deadlock and concurrency problems are intermittent and cannot be reproduced on PGlite.

notes: Cannot be verified locally. A change here can alter what runs on master or what deploys; it needs explicit approval before it is pushed.
Scripts in package.json are what this plan's commands call: check they still exist.
Configures only the online project (including the one-time database setup), so the engine and UI suites cannot be affected. The whole online suite is required: this applies to every online test.
Configures only the engine tests (test/**).
Configures only the UI project.
The root tsconfig is extended by the online project and checked with the engine, so every project is checked.

rules.approval: Database schema, migrations or database access code
notes: Locks, deadlocks and concurrency cannot be verified on PGlite; only CI's PostgreSQL shows them.
A database suite must FAIL (not skip) when CI requires a database: run with CI=true. Never apply schema DDL inside a suite.
Baseline seeds (101-124) must stay disjoint from the test seeds. Re-measure the baseline if the engine's averages deliberately move.
Data and tests the verification tooling reads: they are exercised only by the selector, verdict, safety and replay tests, not by the engine suite.
Standalone arcade module: no franchise imports, database or production entry point. Existing CI is franchise coverage only; arcade evidence must come from its explicit verification command.

Browser tests are not yet a wentz-verify command. Run `npm run e2e:typecheck` and `npm run e2e` (E2E_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome uses an installed Chrome) and report the result as it is. A fixed, allowlisted command is planned for a later change.
The launcher decides which database the real server is started against. A change here must keep an inherited production URL from reaching database initialization: the launcher tests prove it.
A league that cannot leave a stage is only caught by the whole-season walkthroughs.
Result redaction for each GM is built in the league route in index.ts: anything that returns league data must be checked against it.

rules.approval: Simulation balance, model artifacts or player ratings data
notes: The engine loads these files at run time, so no import graph shows who depends on them.

rules.approval: Simulation formulas or balance (any edit that changes game behaviour)
notes: Almost every test imports the engine, so a transitive `related` run is close to the full suite: the full engine suite is required.
Analysis scripts are not run by CI; run the one you changed.
The league server runs these same rules through the `@/` alias, so the online project is checked too.
Shared with the league server through the `@/` alias.
